harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a systemd-managed service `inventory-worker` on node1 running as dedicated unprivileged user `inventory-worker`, sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (plus additional hardening: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, capability/syscall restrictions). Verified via nsenter that writes to /etc and /root are blocked (read-only) while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and running/writing service state, rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service came back active/enabled and resumed writing to its confined directory with sandbox properties intact.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/init (CentOS Stream 10, systemd 257), confirmed root/sudo access
Created system user inventory-worker with home /var/lib/inventory, nologin shell
Created /var/lib/inventory owned by inventory-worker, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh long-running loop that appends inventory data every 10s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User/Group=inventory-worker, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, plus PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices/capability+syscall restrictions
systemctl daemon-reload; enabled and started the service
Verified log growth in /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log
Used nsenter into the service's mount namespace to prove /etc and /root writes fail (read-only) while /var/lib/inventory writes succeed, and confirmed NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<pid>/status
Captured baseline boot_id and service/log state before restart
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 in background so ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed

Verified inventory-worker.service auto-started (enabled+active), resumed logging with reset uptime confirming fresh boot, and sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, ReadWritePaths) persisted post-reboot

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker service exists, is managed by systemd, and runs long-running (writes continuously)
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows active/running service; log file shows periodic timestamped appends

evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory (sandboxing)
evidence.summary: systemctl show confirms ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome=yes/ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory; nsenter into the live process namespace proves writes to /etc and /root fail (read-only) while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes; /proc/<pid>/status inside the running process shows NoNewPrivs: 1
Captured pre-restart boot_id (4d340bf4...), active service state, and growing inventory.log

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot launched backgrounded so the ack ('reboot issued') returned before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Connection failures during reboot window followed by successful exec showing new boot_id 4a185471... (different from baseline) and fresh uptime

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of service, sandbox config, and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: service is active/enabled, log resumed appending (uptime counter reset confirming fresh boot), and sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, ReadWritePaths) intact
